facts.text: Eagle Lake earned its name from a small glacial lake that once covered a quarter of Section 7 and nearby swamps, supplying wild cranberries for Chicago markets.
A post office opened in Eagle Lake in 1865 and closed in 1902, marking the community’s brief 37‑year federal presence.
By the late 19th century, farmers drained the original lake through ditches and tiling, shrinking it to a modest pond and converting wetlands into farmland.
Before settlers, the Potawatomi tribe inhabited the Eagle Lake area, using its prairies, woodlands, and waterways for hunting, fishing, and agriculture.
Eagle Lake enjoys a humid continental climate, with January lows near –7 °C and July highs around 29 °C, and about 41 inches of rain annually.
Eagle Lake is part of the Chicago‑Naperville‑Elgin metropolitan statistical area, linking it to a major economic region.
